data.title: Copart Board Approves Long-Term Stock Option for CEO
data.description:
Copart ( (CPRT) ) has shared an update.

On October 14, 2026, Copart’s board approved a stand‑alone nonstatutory stock option for CEO A. Jayson Adair to purchase 20,000,000 shares, divided into four price‑based tranches, subject to shareholder approval at or after the 2026 annual meeting. The 10‑year option, intended to be Adair’s sole substantive compensation while he receives a nominal $1 annual salary, vests on the fifth anniversary and is structured with clawback, holding period, and detailed death, disability, and change‑in‑control provisions that tightly align CEO rewards with long‑term share price performance and shareholder outcomes.

The grant includes service‑based clawbacks that reclaim 10% of vested shares for each year remaining in the 10‑year term after Adair’s departure, plus mandatory long‑term holding of shares equal to the net exercise gain. Special vesting and waiver rules apply if Adair dies, becomes disabled, or if Copart undergoes a change in control, ensuring that option value is realized only when the stock materially exceeds exercise prices while safeguarding the company’s and shareholders’ interests through compensation recovery mechanisms.
